paraphrase: The imagined, the dependent and the perfected are the three natures, the deep object of the wise. What appears is the dependent, because it occurs in dependence on conditions; how it appears is the imagined, because it is mere imagination; the perfected is the constant non-existence of the appearing thing in the way it appears, because it is never otherwise.

paraphrase: The imagined is both existent and non-existent, since it is grasped as existent and is utterly non-existent; the dependent is both, since it exists as error and does not exist as it appears; the perfected is both, since it exists as non-duality and is the non-existence of duality.
notes: Verse numbering and wording checked against the local GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text (Anacker ed.), transliterated.

paraphrase: The three natures are taught in an order for the sake of convention and of entry: first one enters the dependent as the absence of duality; then one enters it as mere imagination, non-existent duality; then one enters the perfected, the being of the absence of duality — which is therefore said both to exist and not to exist.
notes: Verse numbering and wording checked against the local GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text (Anacker ed.), transliterated.

paraphrase: As a magical illusion produced by the power of a spell appears as an elephant — only the shape is there, the elephant not at all — so the imagined nature is the elephant, the dependent its shape, and the absence of the elephant there is the perfected. Unreal imagination appears from the root mind as duality; the duality does not exist at all; there is only the shape. The root consciousness is like the spell, suchness like the wood, imagination like the elephant's shape, duality like the elephant.

paraphrase: At the penetration of the truth of things, the three characteristics are simultaneously understood, abandoned and attained: understanding is non-apprehension, abandonment is non-appearance, attainment — which is also direct realization — is the apprehension without an image; by not apprehending duality the dual appearance vanishes, and with it the perfected, the absence of duality, is reached — just as in a magic show the non-apprehension of the elephant, the vanishing of its shape and the apprehension of the wood happen at once.
notes: Verse numbering and wording checked against the local GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text (Anacker ed.), transliterated.

paraphrase: Liberation comes without effort through seeing that cognition obstructs the contrary cognition, through seeing the futility (of the object) by understanding, and through the continuation of the three knowledges.
notes: Verse numbering and wording checked against the local GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text (Anacker ed.), transliterated. The verse is compressed; paraphrase follows its three ablatives closely and is to be checked by extraction.

paraphrase: Through the apprehension of mind-only comes the non-apprehension of knowable objects; through the non-apprehension of knowable objects comes the non-apprehension of mind; through the non-apprehension of both comes the apprehension of the dharmadhātu; through the apprehension of the dharmadhātu comes mastery; and having mastery and accomplishing his own and others' aims, the wise one attains unsurpassed awakening, whose nature is the three bodies.

paraphrase: Mind is twofold as cause and effect: the consciousness called ālaya, and the operative consciousness, sevenfold. The first is called 'mind' (citta) because it is accumulated (cita) with the seeds of defilement and imprints; the second because it occurs with variegated (citra) images. Unreal imagination is threefold: maturational (the root consciousness), causal, and appearing (the operative consciousness, seen, seer and seeing).
